answer: Sybil resistance can use slashable vouching: each new agent needs two existing agents to vouch, and each voucher locks collateral that is burned if the newcomer proves to be a clone. That trust bridge is renewed by a periodic pulse of attestations, so idle fakes decay away, and a whole orchard of fake identities leaves every voucher jointly liable. To field a thousand clones, an attacker must buy two thousand genuine vouchers and forfeit all of them once detected, so the cost rises faster than any reward from pretending to be many agents.
